To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) students that do not complete the course tend to have a lower level of participation in the discussion forums, 2) students that do participate in the forums, but do not contribute much to the discussion, are less likely to complete the course and 3) the social network of a student is an important predictor of his/her dropout behavior.

the following factors are significant predictors of dropout: 1) the number of discussion forum posts, 2) the number of replies to posts, 3) the number of different discussion threads, and 4) the number of unique discussion participants in the threads.
students who are active in discussion boards, and who have many friends in the course, are less likely to drop out.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of predictive models for student dropout behavior in MOOCs, and the use of these models to identify students at risk of dropping out.
the question of whether we can predict dropout in MOOCs and if so, how we might do so.
the following questions: What are the factors that predict student dropout?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the social network analysis of student discussion forum data is an important predictor of dropout in Massive Open Online Course.
students who do not engage in the course are more likely to dropout.
the social networks of the learners are not a good predictor for the dropout rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can anticipate dropout behavior in MOOCs using social network analysis and student behavioral data.
we are able to predict student dropout behavior using social network metrics and other student behavioral factors.
students who are more active on discussion forums and who have a higher social status are less likely to dropout.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dropout rate in MOOC is significantly influenced by student behavior and social interactions.
the factors that predict dropout are related to student behavior in the course, not to the student’s background.
the social dimension of the course, as measured by the social network of the discussion forums, has a significant impact on dropout rate.
